 JUDGMENT

This case is arose out of Crime No.026/2016 of Commercial Street Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Section 408 and 420 of IPC based on the gist of facts stated in the FIR which has set this criminal case in motion against the accused.

2. The case of the prosecution is that while the accused working as Sales Executive in Parmananda Hardware shop, bills were fabricated as if the customers taken back the money by returning the purchased hardware material during the period of 01.04.2014 to 30.12.2015.
Thereby, accused had caused loss to the tune of Rs.12,85,044/- to the Parmananda Hardware shop of complainant.
The Commercial Street Police had booked the case against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 408 and 402 of IPC based on the written complaint of Sri. Sunil Ghabha.
The Investigating Officer registered the FIR, prepared the spot panchanama, recorded the statement of witnesses and collected the documents.
Having material in the investigation, Investigating Officer filed charge sheet against the accused for the offences alleged.
4. Upon receipt of the court summons, the accused has entered appearance before the court.
The relevant copies have been furnished under Section 207 of Cr. P.C. to the accused.
The charge for the offence under Section 408 of IPC framed, explained and read over to the accused before the court.
Upon which accused has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried before the court.
5. In the instant case, the prosecution examined CW1 as PW1, CW2 as PW2, CW3 as PW3, CW5 as PW4, CW6 as PW5, CW8 as PW6 and got marked Ex.
P1 to Ex.P220.

Despite issuing summons,
warrants and proclamation warrants, presence of CW4 and CW7 - 4 -- CC-10703/2017 were not secured.
Thereby, CW4 and CW7 were dropped from the charge sheet.
Evidence on prosecution side closed.
6. After closure of the prosecution evidence, the 313 statement was read over and explained to the accused in Kannada language.
The accused has denied the incriminating evidence available on record as false.
The accused has not adduced defence evidence.

7. Heard. Perused the material available on record.
8.

The points that arises for the consideration are :

The findings to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 :- IN THE NEGATIVE  Point No.2:- As per final order for the following:-
 - 5 -- CC-10703/2017  REASONS 10.
Point No.1 :- It is not in dispute that M/s. Parmananda Hardware Retail Store, Commercial Street, Bengaluru owned by complainant carrying on business of architectural hardware and furniture fittings.

Complaint suggests that Vani was working as cashier, Mr. Selvakumar was working as Store Keeper, Mrs. Uma was working as another Cashier and the accused was working as Sales Executive in the Hardware Retail Store of complainant.
Evidence of the complainant suggests that accused was also working in the Bill Section of his Hardware Retail Store.

11. It is stated by the complainant in the evidence that he came to know the two bogus sales return invoices prepared by Vani, on questioning Vani reported that the customers were taken back the money by returning the material, Store Keeper and Sales Executive suppose to look after the sales return, they said that no such material returned back to store room.
Subsequently, Vani disclosed that the accused had instructed to make such entries and handover the money to his custody regularly.

While going through the transactions it was noticed that such sales returns worth of Rs.3,68,000/-, Rs.2,93,000/- and Rs.6,00,000/- were - 6 -- CC-10703/2017 carried by accused by subscribing the signatures on behalf of the Sales Executive and Store Keeper.
12.
It is quite clear from the aforementioned evidence of the complainant that complaint was lodged against the accused based on the statement of the Vani.

Vani did not step into the witness box in Sunil Gaba vs Varunkumar J on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76555570/

sentences.text: Thereby, there is no direct evidence of Vani so as to substantiate that how the accused had committed the offence.
It has come in the evidence of the complainant that Store keeper and Sales Executive informed that there is no return of the goods to the store room.
Store Keeper-Mr. Selvakumar only deposed that he came to know the accused misappropriated the funds of retail store belong to the complainant.
During the course of cross-examination by Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor, he has not given any evidence against the accused.
As such, there is no evidence of Store Keeper so as to demonstrate that there was no such actual sale returns to the store.
It is the say of the complainant that accused had shown in the invoices that the customers were taken back the money by returning the material.
Investigating Officer testified that he did not enquire any of the customers regarding the offence.
The customers interrogation was - 7 -- CC-10703/2017 essential in order to know had the customers really returned the material or otherwise.
There is no evidence to the effect that any of the particular customers referred to the accused while he was performing duty as a Sales Executive.
It has come in the evidence of the complainant that one of the lady cashier complaint against the accused.
It pre-supposes that cashier is none other than employee of his retail shop.
As such, the complainant must have disclosed the name of the cashier who made allegations against the accused.
When such is the case, say of the complainant shall be construed as vague.
Complainant has stated that Store Keeper and Sales Executive verify the books and take that sales return but no complaints were received from the sales executive.
As I stated earlier, Store Keeper did not support the case of the prosecution.
Complainant clearly admits that when the customers return the material they will be referred to the respective Sales Executives.
If in case, there was no proper sales returns there must be some complaints from the Sales Returns Section.
The complainant made it clear that no such complaints were received from the Sales Executives.
The complainant has volunteered that there are separate sections for sales plus sales return and cash.
One person is in-charge of the Sales plus Sales returns of customers and six to - 8 -- CC-10703/2017 eight employees work in the Sales and Sales returns section,
When there were several Sales Executives in the retail shop of the complainant how he particularly concluded that accused indulged in the commission of the offence is unanswered.
According to the testimony of the Investigating Officer he did not record the statements of the persons working in the sales returns section.
Persons working in the sales returns section through light on why there was no proper sales return to the store.
In fact, Investigating Officer failed to record the statements of the persons working in the sales returns section.
Such a missing evidence fail to connect the accused with crime.

13. Though it is found in the complaint that Vani did such transaction since the accused forced her to co-operate with him and the accused said that she will be safe in the work place otherwise she will have to face the dire consequences but such material fact that Vani did alleged transaction due to pressure of the accused missing the evidence of the complainant.
It is the version of the complainant that Vani was undergoing training with the accused and that the accused not only doing work as sales executive but also he was working in the billing section.
One of

sentences.text: When the evidence suggests that accused has no full knowledge about billing, Vani said to be working under the instructions of accused is suspicious.
So the criminal liability cannot be fasten against the accused.

14. Complainant has deposed that every day he monitor the financial transactions but he came to know the financial irregularities only in the month of December 2015, they conduct the financial audit every year but no such loss of Rs.12,85,000/- reflected in audit report and they never conduct stock verification report.
Investigating Officer deposed that he made letter correspondence with complainant but he has not furnished the audit report or stock verification report.

Aforementioned evidence complainant clearly indicates that all the allegations made against the accused relying on the version of the Vani but it has not been supported by any cogent proof such as audit report or stock verification report, if in case complainant is regularly monitoring the transactions why there was delay in detecting the financial irregularities has not been explained.

Complainant tendered evidence that the accused subscribed his signature by using different names in different languages on invoices in 80% of the transactions and accused insisted Vani to sign the invoices and hand over money to his custody in another 20% of the transactions.
Series of invoices have been marked as Ex.P51 to 209.
Signatures of the customers and authorized signatories are found in the invoices placed before the court.
Investigating Officer never made an attempt to procure the admitted and disputed signatures and get the handwriting expert report so as to prove that accused had fabricated those invoices/bills.
Under such circumstances, there are no enough material evidence to hold that the accused had shown the customers were taken back the material without actually returning the material in the invoices.
One more employee of retail shop of complainant by name Sathish deposed that he came to know that the accused misappropriated the funds in the retail shop of the complainant.
It is a hear say evidence of Sathish.
Sathish and R.Vinayakaswamy testified that the police have drawn the spot panchanama in the hardware retail store of the complainant.

In the absence of cogent evidence regarding the commission of the offence by the accused, the evidences of the panch witnesses - 11- - CC-10703/2017 regarding the spot panchanama will not in any way helpful to the case of the prosecution.
That apart, Sathish admits that he signed the spot panchanama as instructed by the police and he had no knowledge about the spot panchanama.
So the evidence of the Sathish regarding spot panchanama is shaky.
16. Complainant said that the police have not seized money from the custody of the accused.
Investigating Officer said that the bank statement of the accused was not collected during the course of investigation.
These aspects are very much important to understand had the accused mis-utilized the funds retail shop of the complainant for his personal benefit.
This missing piece of evidence do fail to connect the accused with crime.

Accordingly, accused is entitled for acquittal of the offences alleged.
Hence, I record findings on Point No.1 in the NEGATIVE.

18. Point No.2:- For the reasons discussed in the Point No.1, I pass the following:
 - 12- - CC-10703/2017  ORDER
In exercise of power conferred under Section 248(1) of Cr. P.C. accused found not guilty of the offences punishable under Section 408 of IPC.

The bail bond and surety bond of the accused is extended for a period of 6 months in compliance of Section 437(A) of Cr. P.C.
